# Waiting logs are parsed once per file version: an in-process cache keyed by inode, size and mtime…

Waiting logs are parsed once per file version: an in-process cache keyed by inode, size and mtime holds each log's items and step rows; callers get shallow copies

**Context.** The #116 spike measured `waitingSteps` at 41 of 160 ms of a changed Home refresh in dirtywork. A panel draw calls it two or three times (draw, `inboxNow`, `inboxParts`), and every call re-read and re-parsed every session log, though usually at most one log changed since the last draw.

**Decision.** `waiting.js` keeps a module-level map: log path → `{key, items, steps}`, where key = `ino:size:mtimeMs`. `parsedLogs(root)` lists the folder, stats each `.jsonl`, and reparses only logs whose key changed; logs gone from the folder are dropped from the map. `waitingItems` and `waitingSteps` build from it; step rows are made once per log version (`stepsOf`) and sorted per call. Callers get shallow copies of items and rows, so a caller that sets a field does not change the cache.

**Why this key.** Hooks only append (size grows). The archive and other rewriters write a new file (new inode) or change the size. A same-size, same-mtime, same-inode rewrite is the only miss, and it does not happen in practice.

**Not done.** A worker (no-go in #116). Caching `openSteps`/`itemsOf` callers in hooks: each hook runs in its own short process, so a cache there buys nothing.

Alternative: a worker thread, rejected because the #116 spike found it was not worth it (no-go).
Alternative: caching in the hooks that call `openSteps`/`itemsOf`, rejected because each hook runs in its own short-lived process, so a cache there buys nothing.
